title: Additive manufacturing of ultralong and architected single crystals
title_zh: 超长及架构化单晶的增材制造
abstract: Single-crystal materials are indispensable for high-performance applications, yet their deployment remains constrained by conventional manufacturing techniques that depend on strict quasi-steady thermal conditions1. This requirement fundamentally conflicts with the intense cyclic thermal fluctuations inherent to additive manufacturing2, historically preventing the 3D printing of large or architected single crystals. Here we present a free-form additive manufacturing approach that resolves this contradiction by using delicately controlled alternating and pulsed heat inputs to govern and direct single-crystal growth. Using this method, we demonstrate the fabrication of metre-tall, centimetre-diameter single-crystal Ti-6Al-4V alongside, to our knowledge, the first single-crystal lattice structures containing complex zigzag ligaments, effectively eliminating theoretical size constraints for single-crystal components. The resulting bulk single-crystal Ti-6Al-4V exhibits an order-of-magnitude increase in creep resistance over standard grain-size scaling predictions, driven by the synergistic elimination of grain boundaries and an additive manufacturing-induced hierarchical α/β-architecture that regulates dislocation density, mobility and void evolution. Furthermore, we demonstrate the broad applicability of this technique by printing single crystals of hard-to-process refractory metals, including W, Mo, Nb and MoNb alloys. Our work introduces a large-scale method for single-crystal additive manufacturing, expanding the accessible materials library and enabling high-performance, complex geometries previously unattainable by classical methods. A free-form additive manufacturing method that uses alternating and pulsed heat inputs is described for fabricating metre-tall, centimetre-diameter single crystals of Ti-6Al-4V, as well as hard-to-process refractory metals, including W, Mo, Nb and MoNb alloys.
abstract_zh: 单晶材料对于高性能应用不可或缺，但其应用仍受依赖严格准稳态热条件的传统制造技术所限制。这一要求与增材制造固有的强烈循环热波动根本冲突，此前历史上阻碍了大尺寸或架构化单晶的3D打印。我们提出了一种自由成形的增材制造方法，通过精心控制的交替和脉冲热输入来引导和控制单晶生长，从而解决这一矛盾。利用该方法，我们展示了制造米高、厘米直径的单晶Ti-6Al-4V，以及据我们所知首个含复杂之字韧带的单晶晶格结构，实际上消除了单晶元件的理论尺寸限制。所得块状单晶Ti-6Al-4V的蠕变抗力较标准晶粒尺寸缩放预测提高了一个数量级，这是由晶界协同消除以及增材制造诱导的分层α/β结构所驱动，该结构调节位错密度、位错迁移和空洞演化。此外，我们还展示了该技术的广泛适用性，打印了难加工的耐火金属单晶，包括W、Mo、Nb及MoNb合金。我们的工作引入了一种大规模的单晶增材制造方法，扩大了可获取的材料库，并实现了经典方法难以达成的高性能复杂几何结构。本文描述了一种采用交替和脉冲热输入的自由成形增材制造方法，用于制备米高、厘米直径的Ti-6Al-4V单晶，以及W、Mo、Nb和MoNb合金等难加工耐火金属。
